title: Enterprise Onboarding Preflight - KMS, Egress & SLA Mapping
summary: Preflight between Redwood AE/SE and Triton to align contract routing (MSA/DPA), KMS/egress requirements, SLA mapping for enterprise deployment options and pricing approval path. Agreed to run a short hosted-to-private POC and prepare a redlines memo for legal.
topics: MSA / DPA redlines and legal path
KMS integrations and customer key options
Network egress / VPC peering and data residency
SLA tiers and latency targets for trading workloads
Pricing approval path and pilot scope
Next steps: security docs, benchmark run, legal memo
next_steps: Redwood to share SOC 2 / ISO summary + KMS integration doc by 2027-03-10
SE to schedule 1-hour benchmark window next week (hosted and dedicated) by 2027-03-12
Maya to send draft MSA redlines template and proposed SLA mappings to Sofia by 2027-03-11
Triton to confirm procurement timeline and decision committee members by 2027-03-15
action_items: Ethan Ruiz: prepare benchmark plan (latency p95, cold-start, token cost) - due 2027-03-12
Maya Patel: email MSA/DPA redlines and pricing pathway to Sofia and Jared - due 2027-03-11
Anika Rao: provide KMS policy and egress constraints (IP allowlist / peering) - due 2027-03-10
Priya Nand: compile success criteria for pilot (throughput, cost per 1M tokens, security gates) - due 2027-03-14
transcript:
Header:
Date: 2027-03-07
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Lena (CS), Jared (Triton Procurement), Sofia (Triton Legal), Anika (Triton Security), Marcus (Triton DevOps), Priya (Product)

[00:00] Maya: hey everyone thanks for jumping on, i know this is the preflight ahead of your procurement loop so we'll try to be succinct. Um quick roll call?
[00:12] Jared: Jared here, sofia, anika, marcus, priya all on. thanks, maya.
[00:18] Maya: great. ethan i'll hand to you for a quick technical set so folks know the vector of discussion?
[00:24] Ethan: yeah thanks. so high level redwood supports hosted, dedicated and private (vpc/on-prem) deployments. for this call i want to focus on two lines: key management - customer keys via KMS/HSM and egress/networking - how requests and data stay in region. also brief SLA mapping for low-latency trading style use cases.
[00:42] Marcus: just to flag, our latency SLO for trade suggester is p95 < 120ms for in-app calls, that includes our client libraries and rounding. curious how that maps to your hosted offering.
[00:56] Ethan: yes this is common ask; hosted with our optimized runtime can hit p95 around 80–150ms depending on model and sequence length. dedicated gives stronger tail guarantees because of reserved GPU capacity, and private (VPC) gets you control over network egress but adds a touch of infra overhead.
[01:18] Sofia: for legal, high level, two things: our legal team needs to see MSA and DPA redlines and a clear escalation and audit trail for data access. also, provisioning of a customer-managed key is a hard requirement for PCI-adjacent workloads.
[01:34] Maya: absolutely. we have a KMS flow that supports both bring-your-own-key (BYOK) via customer KMS and an HSM-backed option in private deployments. i'll flag lena to follow up with the KMS integration doc.
[01:46] Lena: happy to. i'll share the integration matrix with key rotation cadence, supported providers (aws-kms, gcp-kms, azure-keyvault) — and note about wrapped keys for on-prem.
[02:02] Anika: on the egress side, we need deterministic egress IPs for firewall rules and optionally VPC peering, plus retention controls: we can't allow raw customer PII to be stored beyond 30 days. how do you handle prefix caching and KV cache retention?
[02:20] Ethan: good call. prefix/KV caching is configurable and in enterprise plans we can disable persistent KV caching or set TTLs — ephemeral cache for session-only use cases. we also provide audit logs per-request and per-token level metadata in the console.
[02:38] Priya: what's the difference in audit log retention between hosted and private? we have a compliance window that requires 13 months for certain events.
[02:46] Lena: hosted default is 90 days; enterprise add-ons bump that to 13 months or longer; private deployment you control retention (on customer infra). we'll include retention tiers in the doc.
[02:58] Jared: okay procurement question — pricing: if we start with a hosted pilot then commit to dedicated for production, how's the path to pricing approval? we need a clean TCO and concessional pricing for committed reserved capacity.
[03:12] Maya: typical flow: pilot (hosted) -> benchmark -> pilot results + SLOs -> procurement commits to reserved capacity (Redwood Dedicated) with monthly/annual commit options. we'll supply model-specific cost breakdowns and a recommended commit level. pricing approvals often require an internal business case; we'll help with a cost model spreadsheet.
[03:34] Marcus: can that spreadsheet show per-token units and also GPU-hour equivalents? our finance folks like both views.
[03:40] Maya: yes we'll add both.
[03:42] Sofia: legal redlines — we need clarity around data processing, subprocessor list, and egress assistance in the event of a data subject request. do you have a standard DPA with subprocessors called out?
[03:54] Maya: we do and we'll attach the current subprocessor list; we also can agree to narrow subprocessors in enterprise DPA variants. if there's a need for a Data Processing Impact Assessment we can work with your privacy team.
[04:08] Sofia: and about forensic access: in some cases regulators want full request logs including request payloads, how is that handled?
[04:16] Ethan: by default we log metadata and redacted payloads; for sensitive cases with a private deployment we can provide additional logs stored under customer control. we can put controls in the DPA with specified access procedures — and tie that to KMS policies so only your key can decrypt certain artifacts.
[04:34] Anika: ok good. we also need to confirm SOC 2 type II and ISO certs, and any pen test reports.
[04:42] Lena: we will share SOC 2 Type II attestation and latest penetration test summary. full reports may require an NDA, but summary and controls mapping is standard.
[04:52] Priya: about pilot success criteria, our product team wants throughput of 200 req/sec with median latency < 60ms for short prompts, cost under $X per 1M tokens — that's a target not a hard requirement yet.
[05:08] Ethan: noted. for those numbers we'll design the benchmark with sequence length distribution and concurrency to replicate peak traffic.
[05:16] Jared: procurement timeline — we aim for committee review in two weeks, final sign-off by end of month. can you commit to providing legal and security docs swiftly?
[05:26] Maya: yes will prioritize, target delivery dates in next steps.

[05:40] -- deep dive: KMS / keying options --
[05:44] Ethan: two patterns: hosted BYOK where customer stores master key in their KMS and we request wrapped keys; or private where customer hosts whole control plane and keys never leave their network. hosted BYOK still requires a trust boundary because wrapped keys are used with our runtime — if regulator requires no external key use we'll recommend private deployment.
[06:10] Anika: do you support HSM attestation? we need to ensure keys are generated in an FIPS 140-2 level 3 device for certain workloads.
[06:18] Ethan: we support KMS providers that back onto HSMs; for private on-prem we can integrate with customer HSMs directly. we can capture attestation statements where supported.
[06:26] Sofia: so legal acceptance depends on that attestation and the DPA clause. if we can't get attestation for hosted we'll ask for private.

[06:40] -- networking / egress --
[06:44] Marcus: can you provide static egress IPs for firewall allowlisting or do you require VPC peering only?
[06:52] Ethan: both. hosted offers static egress IP ranges (enterprise tier); peering is available for dedicated and private. for hosted static IPs we publish them and update with notification windows.
[07:04] Marcus: update windows are important; we have strict firewall policies. can you guarantee no mid-day changes without 30-day notice?
[07:12] Maya: we can commit to 30-day notice for IP range changes in enterprise contracts. we'll add that to SLA mapping.

[07:26] -- SLA discussion --
[07:28] Priya: show of hands, what SLA tiers do you offer and what does the remediation look like?
[07:34] Lena: typical tiers: standard (99.9 uptime, best-effort latency), enterprise (99.95, priority support), premium (99.99, dedicated capacity options). remedies range from service credits to escalation paths and optional runbooks for failover.
[07:52] Ethan: for low-latency workloads we recommend dedicated pools with pinned instances to reduce variability; fallback to a lower-cost model variant is supported for graceful degradation.
[08:04] Marcus: what about SLA for tail latency? we need p95/p99 commitments not just uptime.
[08:10] Ethan: tail latency commitments are possible on dedicated/premium but they come with capacity reservation and defined workload profiles; we'll specify p95/p99 on the SLA mapping doc per model and sequence length.

[08:24] -- pricing path and procurement questions --
[08:28] Jared: assuming a 12-month commit on dedicated, what's the expected discount band?
[08:34] Maya: depends on commit size; typical bands: 15–35% off hosted list for mid-tier commits, higher for multi-year. we'll propose bands in the pricing sheet and show best-fit for your forecast.
[08:48] Jared: procurement will need a comparison vs another vendor (CloudVendorX) — they push a cheaper per-token but higher egress fees. can you show a total cost of ownership?
[08:58] Maya: yes we'll include per-token, egress, and a GPU-equivalent line.

[09:12] -- legal redlines and timeline --
[09:16] Sofia: for the MSA we have a handful of non-negotiables: data locality, KMS BYOK, audit access, indemnities limited to X (redacted in notes), and a standard 60-day termination clause with data return assistance. we'll circulate a redline doc.
[09:32] Maya: fine. we'll accept limited negotiation on subprocessor terms but need to protect core IP clauses. we'll also provide a standard data return playbook for offboarding.
[09:44] Sofia: ok also DPA: need to call out processors, cross-border flows, and delete-on-demand for PII subject requests.
[09:54] Lena: we'll include explicit DPA sections for delete-on-demand and DSAR workflow.

[10:06] -- benchmark planning --
[10:10] Ethan: plan: 2-hour hosted run with synthetic traffic, measure p50/p95/p99, cold start and steady state; then a dedicated run (if you provision) or simulated via reserved test pool. we'll instrument token-cost per model variant.
[10:26] Marcus: window needs to be outside market open hours; we'll propose 02:00–04:00 ET slot.
[10:34] Ethan: ok we'll suggest times in the scheduling thread.

[10:40] -- risk and mitigations --
[10:44] Anika: risk we see: vendor access to raw payloads and potential leak. mitigation?
[10:50] Ethan: mitigation layers: KMS BYOK, restricted admin roles, per-request encryption, logging to customer-owned sinks for private deployments. we can also do a SOC controls mapping exercise.
[11:04] Sofia: we may ask for a contractual clause limiting Redwood to process data only for delivery of services and subject to audit rights.
[11:12] Maya: yes that's standard, we'll add the language.

[11:24] -- edge cases: incident response and legal subpoena flow --
[11:28] Jared: if there's a subpoena requesting customer data, what's your process?
[11:34] Lena: we send notice to the customer where permitted, follow our legal response playbook. for private deployments it's customer-controlled. we'll include specifics in the DPA.

[11:46] -- closing and recaps --
[11:50] Maya: quick recap: Redwood to share SOC 2/ISO summaries, KMS integration doc, pricing TCO spreadsheet and MSA redline template. Ethan to run benchmark plan, schedule with Marcus. Triton to supply KMS policy and firewall requirements. legal to produce initial redline and we'll sync on timelines.
[12:12] Sofia: sounds good, small ask — please mark any clauses that are vendor standard vs negotiable in the redline so we don't go back and forth on trivial items.
[12:22] Maya: will do, we'll annotate the redline.
[12:26] Marcus: one last note — can dedicated capacity be staged regionally? we need eu + na footprint.
[12:32] Ethan: yes dedicated can be multi-region with separate pools; we will show regional latency and cost delta in the TCO.
[12:40] Priya: thanks everyone — can we lock a follow-up in two weeks for procurement committee?
[12:46] Jared: yes aiming for 2027-03-21.
[12:50] Maya: I'll send calendar invite. thanks all.

[12:58] -- end of recording: call wraps with action items and next steps captured --

Notes on transcription: occasional speaker attribution errors (e.g., anika/sofia lines), filler words preserved, some technical acronyms spelled out inconsistently (KMS, KV cache, VPC).
